title: Patient Safety
outline: NAHQ CPHQ Detailed Content Outline (2024 R2b, in 2026 handbook)

questions.task_name: Identify technology solutions to enhance patient safety
questions.stem: Which error type is barcode medication administration (BCMA) PRIMARILY designed to prevent?

options.A: Bedside administration errors (wrong patient or drug)
options.B: Prescribing errors caused by incorrect dose selection by physicians
options.C: Drug procurement errors
options.D: Errors in pharmacy inventory counts and expiry date tracking

questions.explanation_en: BCMA verifies patient and medication at the point of administration. Prescribing errors are addressed mainly by CPOE with decision support. Workarounds (e.g., scanning copied labels) defeat BCMA.
questions.explanation_ar: نظام الباركود يمنع أخطاء الإعطاء مثل المريض أو الدواء الخطأ.

questions.task_name: Identify technology solutions to enhance patient safety
questions.stem: Physicians override 92% of CPOE drug-interaction alerts. What is the BEST action?

options.A: Make every drug-interaction alert a hard stop that cannot be overridden
options.B: Refine alert logic to cut low-value alerts and alert fatigue
options.C: Discipline high overriders
options.D: Turn off all interaction alerts, since physicians ignore them anyway

questions.explanation_en: Very high override rates signal alert fatigue; tuning alerts preserves attention for important warnings. Hard stops for all alerts create workarounds; turning all off removes protection.
questions.explanation_ar: ارتفاع تجاوز التنبيهات يدل على إجهاد التنبيهات؛ حسّن منطقها.

questions.task_name: Identify technology solutions to enhance patient safety
questions.stem: Smart infusion pumps reduce infusion errors MOST effectively when:

options.A: Nurses bypass it for urgent infusions
options.B: The pumps are used only in the ICU where nurses are most experienced
options.C: The drug library with dose limits is used consistently
options.D: Pump alarms are silenced during night shifts to reduce noise for patients

questions.explanation_en: Smart pump safety depends on drug-library compliance; bypassing it ('basic mode') removes dose-limit protection. Library compliance is itself a useful monitoring measure.
questions.explanation_ar: مضخات التسريب الذكية فعالة عند الالتزام بمكتبة الأدوية.

questions.task_name: Apply techniques to enhance the culture of safety within the organization
questions.stem: A nurse skipped a required independent double-check because unit norms treat it as optional when busy. No harm occurred. Using Just Culture, how should this be managed?

options.A: Console the nurse, because skipping the check was an inadvertent slip
options.B: Impose disciplinary action, because this was clearly reckless behavior
options.C: No action, since no harm occurred
options.D: Coach the nurse and fix the norm that made the drift acceptable

questions.explanation_en: Choosing to drift from a rule because the risk is not recognized or seems justified is at-risk behavior → coaching plus fixing incentives/system. Human error → console; reckless (conscious disregard of substantial risk) → sanction. Outcome should not determine the response.
questions.explanation_ar: الانحراف عن القاعدة سلوك محفوف بالمخاطر يتطلب التوجيه وإصلاح النظام.

questions.task_name: Apply techniques to enhance the culture of safety within the organization
questions.stem: Which tool is used to measure staff perceptions of patient safety culture?

options.A: AHRQ Surveys on Patient Safety Culture (SOPS)
options.B: HCAHPS hospital patient experience survey
options.C: IHI Global Trigger Tool for adverse events
options.D: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) worksheet

questions.explanation_en: SOPS (formerly HSOPS) measures staff perceptions of safety culture. HCAHPS measures patient experience; the Global Trigger Tool detects adverse events; FMEA is a proactive risk assessment.
questions.explanation_ar: استبيانات AHRQ SOPS تقيس ثقافة السلامة لدى الموظفين.

questions.task_name: Apply techniques to enhance the culture of safety within the organization
questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a brief daily safety huddle?

options.A: Conduct a full root cause analysis of yesterday's reported events
options.B: Share current safety concerns and anticipate risks for the day
options.C: Review the monthly unit budget
options.D: Assign responsibility and blame for the previous day's safety events

questions.explanation_en: Safety huddles are short, frequent, forward-looking situational awareness tools that escalate concerns quickly. Deep analysis happens elsewhere; blame undermines reporting.
questions.explanation_ar: اجتماع السلامة اليومي القصير لمشاركة المخاطر الحالية والمتوقعة.

questions.task_name: Use safety principles (human factors, high reliability, high-performance teams, systems thinking)
questions.stem: Following an event, several actions are proposed. Which is the STRONGEST according to the action hierarchy?

options.A: Re-educate all nursing staff on tubing safety at the next skills fair
options.B: Write a new policy requiring two-person checks of tubing connections
options.C: Redesign connectors so wrong tubing cannot connect
options.D: Add a warning label to tubing

questions.explanation_en: Stronger actions are architectural/physical changes and forcing functions that do not rely on memory or vigilance. Training, policies and warnings are weaker actions.
questions.explanation_ar: إعادة تصميم الوصلات بحيث يستحيل الخطأ هو الإجراء الأقوى.

questions.task_name: Use safety principles (human factors, high reliability, high-performance teams, systems thinking)
questions.stem: A junior nurse voices concern that a patient is deteriorating, and the team pauses the procedure to reassess. Which high-reliability principle does this BEST illustrate?

options.A: Deference to expertise
options.B: Reluctance to simplify
options.C: Commitment to resilience
options.D: Preoccupation with failure

questions.explanation_en: Deference to expertise means decisions migrate to the person with the most relevant knowledge, regardless of rank. The other principles are valid HRO principles but describe different behaviors.
questions.explanation_ar: الاحترام للخبرة يعني أن القرار لصاحب المعرفة لا لصاحب الرتبة.

questions.task_name: Use safety principles (human factors, high reliability, high-performance teams, systems thinking)
questions.stem: A physician orders '0.5 mg' and the nurse repeats back '0.5 mg IV now, correct?' and the physician confirms. Which TeamSTEPPS technique is this?

options.A: SBAR structured situation report
options.B: Two-challenge rule for raising concerns
options.C: CUS escalation ('concerned, uncomfortable, safety')
options.D: Check-back (closed-loop communication)

questions.explanation_en: Check-back closes the communication loop: sender → receiver repeats → sender confirms. SBAR structures a report; two-challenge rule and CUS are assertion/escalation tools.
questions.explanation_ar: إعادة التأكيد (Check-back) تغلق حلقة التواصل.

questions.task_name: Use safety principles (human factors, high reliability, high-performance teams, systems thinking)
questions.stem: In the 'Swiss cheese' model of accident causation, latent conditions are BEST described as:

options.A: Errors made by the person at the sharp end at the time of the event
options.B: Hidden system weaknesses that combine with active failures
options.C: Patients' underlying diseases and comorbidities that raise their risk
options.D: Deliberate policy violations

questions.explanation_en: Reason's model distinguishes active failures (sharp end, immediate) from latent conditions (blunt end: design, management decisions, workload) that create holes in defenses.
questions.explanation_ar: الظروف الكامنة نقاط ضعف خفية في النظام تتحد مع الأخطاء النشطة.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: safety event/incident reporting
questions.stem: After a manager publicly disciplined staff for reported errors, incident reports dropped 40%. What is the MOST likely interpretation?

options.A: Safety has improved
options.B: The reporting system is working well and needs no change
options.C: Under-reporting due to fear, not safer care
options.D: Staff are now more competent after the disciplinary action

questions.explanation_en: Report volume reflects reporting culture. A sudden drop after punitive responses suggests reduced psychological safety. Higher reporting with lower harm is generally a healthy sign.
questions.explanation_ar: انخفاض البلاغات بعد العقاب يعني نقص الإبلاغ خوفاً لا تحسن السلامة.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: safety event/incident reporting
questions.stem: Pharmacy dispenses the wrong medication; the nurse notices it before administration. How is this event classified?

options.A: Near miss (good catch)
options.B: Adverse event with harm
options.C: Sentinel event requiring review
options.D: No-harm event that reached the patient

questions.explanation_en: A near miss does not reach the patient. A no-harm event reaches the patient without harm; an adverse event causes harm; a sentinel event involves death, permanent harm, or severe temporary harm.
questions.explanation_ar: الخطأ الذي اكتُشف قبل وصوله للمريض حدث وشيك (Near miss).

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: sentinel/unexpected event review
questions.stem: Within what timeframe does The Joint Commission expect an organization to complete a comprehensive systematic analysis and action plan after becoming aware of a sentinel event?

options.A: 24 hours after the event
options.B: 7 calendar days after discovery
options.C: 6 months after the event occurred
options.D: 45 business days

questions.explanation_en: TJC expects the comprehensive systematic analysis (e.g., RCA) and corrective action plan within 45 business days of the event or of becoming aware of it. Immediate patient-safety actions should of course be taken right away.
questions.explanation_ar: التحليل وخطة العمل للحدث الجسيم خلال 45 يوم عمل.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: root cause analysis
questions.stem: Which is NOT a characteristic of a well-conducted root cause analysis?

options.A: It focuses on systems and processes rather than on individual blame
options.B: It aims to find the individual to discipline
options.C: It repeatedly asks 'why'
options.D: It produces corrective actions with measures of their effectiveness

questions.explanation_en: RCA looks for system-level contributing causes and actionable fixes. Blame-focused reviews suppress reporting and miss latent conditions.
questions.explanation_ar: تحليل السبب الجذري يركز على النظام لا على معاقبة الأفراد.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: root cause analysis
questions.stem: Which causal statement follows recommended RCA rules?

options.A: The nurse was careless and forgot to pass on the critical lab result during the handoff
options.B: Poor communication between the night and day teams caused the delayed treatment event
options.C: No standard handoff tool made it likely the pending result was missed, delaying treatment
options.D: The physician should have checked the pending lab result before leaving the hospital

questions.explanation_en: Good causal statements show cause → effect → event, avoid negative descriptors ('careless', 'poor'), and identify a preceding cause for each human error. Blaming individuals is not a causal statement.
questions.explanation_ar: بيان السبب الجيد يربط السبب بالأثر بالحدث دون لوم.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: proactive risk assessment
questions.stem: In an FMEA, a failure mode is rated Severity = 8, Occurrence = 3, Detection = 5. What is the Risk Priority Number (RPN)?
questions.explanation_en: RPN = Severity × Occurrence × Detection = 8 × 3 × 5 = 120. (Adding the values gives 16; S×D = 40; S×O = 24.)
questions.explanation_ar: رقم أولوية الخطر = الشدة × الحدوث × الاكتشاف = 120.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: proactive risk assessment
questions.stem: An FMEA team finds a failure mode with a moderate RPN but a severity score of 10 (catastrophic). What should the team do?

options.A: Prioritize mitigating it despite its lower RPN
options.B: Ignore it, because only the top-ranked RPN items are addressed in an FMEA
options.C: Lower the severity score so that it is consistent with the calculated RPN
options.D: Wait until it happens, then do an RCA

questions.explanation_en: RPN ranking can hide catastrophic but rare failures. Best practice is to also address any failure mode with very high severity regardless of RPN.
questions.explanation_ar: عالج نمط الفشل شديد الخطورة حتى لو لم يكن رقمه الأعلى.

questions.task_name: Facilitate the ongoing evaluation of safety activities
questions.stem: Compared with voluntary incident reporting, the IHI Global Trigger Tool typically:

options.A: Finds many more adverse events via structured chart review
options.B: Finds fewer events because it relies entirely on voluntary staff reports
options.C: It measures safety culture
options.D: Replaces the need for root cause analysis of serious safety events

questions.explanation_en: Trigger-based chart review detects far more harm than voluntary reports, which capture only a small fraction of events. It measures harm rates; it does not measure culture or replace RCA.
questions.explanation_ar: أداة المحفزات العالمية تكشف أحداثاً ضارة أكثر من البلاغات الطوعية.

questions.task_name: Facilitate the ongoing evaluation of safety activities
questions.stem: How should the effectiveness of an RCA action plan BEST be evaluated?

options.A: Confirm the plan was approved
options.B: Track process and outcome measures until sustained
options.C: Count the number of staff who attended the related training sessions
options.D: Assume the plan succeeded if no complaints are received in six months

questions.explanation_en: Action-plan effectiveness requires measurable process and outcome indicators with targets and timelines. Approval or attendance shows activity, not effect.
questions.explanation_ar: فعالية خطة العمل تُقاس بمؤشرات العملية والنتيجة عبر الزمن.

questions.task_name: Integrate safety concepts throughout the organization
questions.stem: After a patient is harmed by a medical error, what is the recommended approach to communication with the patient and family?

options.A: Wait until the legal review is fully complete before any discussion
options.B: Disclose only if asked directly
options.C: Prompt, honest disclosure, apology, and follow-up
options.D: Have the involved clinician send a brief written note to the family only

questions.explanation_en: Communication-and-resolution approaches (e.g., CANDOR) support early, transparent disclosure, empathy/apology, investigation updates, and support for patients and staff. Delay and silence erode trust.
questions.explanation_ar: الإفصاح الصادق والسريع مع الاعتذار والمتابعة هو النهج الموصى به.

questions.task_name: Identify technology solutions to enhance patient safety
questions.stem: CPOE with clinical decision support is MOST likely to prevent which error?

options.A: Ordering a drug the patient is documented as allergic to
options.B: Dispensing a look-alike vial from the wrong automated cabinet bin
options.C: Programming errors on a smart infusion pump at the bedside
options.D: Giving a correctly ordered medication to the wrong patient at the bedside

questions.explanation_en: CPOE/CDS targets the prescribing stage with allergy, dose, and interaction checks.
questions.explanation_ar: نظام الطلب الإلكتروني مع دعم القرار يمنع أخطاء الوصف مثل الحساسية.

questions.task_name: Identify technology solutions to enhance patient safety
questions.stem: After BCMA implementation, nurses print extra patient wristbands and tape them to the medication cart to scan. What does this MOST likely indicate?

options.A: A pharmacy dispensing error
options.B: A training issue only, solved by repeating BCMA education for nurses
options.C: Excellent compliance with BCMA, since every dose is still being scanned
options.D: A workaround signaling a design or workflow problem

questions.explanation_en: Workarounds defeat the safety technology and point to usability or workflow failures to fix.
questions.explanation_ar: الالتفاف على النظام يدل على مشكلة في التصميم يجب دراستها.

questions.task_name: Identify technology solutions to enhance patient safety
questions.stem: Before implementing a new EHR alert for sepsis, what should the safety team do to reduce unintended consequences?

options.A: Turn it on hospital-wide immediately so no septic patient is missed
options.B: Make it a hard stop for all patients
options.C: Test with users and monitor false positives after go-live
options.D: Hide it from nurses so that only physicians receive the sepsis alert

questions.explanation_en: Technology introduces new risks; usability testing and post-implementation monitoring reduce them.
questions.explanation_ar: اختبر التنبيه مع المستخدمين وراقب الإنذارات الكاذبة بعد التشغيل.

questions.task_name: Facilitate the ongoing evaluation of safety activities
questions.stem: Fall-prevention compliance audits show 95% bundle use, yet the fall-with-injury rate has not changed in a year. What is the BEST next step?

options.A: Increase the frequency of compliance audits without other changes
options.B: Declare the program successful because bundle compliance is 95%
options.C: Stop measuring falls because the bundle is already being followed
options.D: Check whether the bundle targets the real causes and audits are valid

questions.explanation_en: When process measures look good but outcomes do not move, check the measure validity and the theory of change.
questions.explanation_ar: إذا لم تتحسن النتيجة رغم الالتزام، راجع صحة القياس وملاءمة الإجراءات.

questions.task_name: Facilitate the ongoing evaluation of safety activities
questions.stem: Which measure BEST evaluates the effectiveness of a new hand-off tool implemented to reduce communication errors?

options.A: Number of tool copies printed
options.B: Handoff-related events and near misses before and after
options.C: Hours of training delivered on the new handoff tool this quarter
options.D: Number of staff who signed the new handoff policy acknowledgment

questions.explanation_en: Effectiveness is shown by outcome and process change, not activities.
questions.explanation_ar: قِس الأحداث المرتبطة بالتسليم قبل وبعد التطبيق.

questions.task_name: Facilitate the ongoing evaluation of safety activities
questions.stem: Which is a balancing measure for a project to reduce ICU length of stay?

options.A: ICU length of stay
options.B: Number of ICU beds
options.C: ICU readmission within 48 hours
options.D: Nurse satisfaction survey response rate

questions.explanation_en: Balancing measures detect unintended harm elsewhere, such as early discharge leading to readmission.
questions.explanation_ar: مقياس التوازن يكشف الأثر غير المقصود مثل إعادة الدخول للعناية.

questions.task_name: Apply techniques to enhance the culture of safety within the organization
questions.stem: A nurse knowingly turned off a bed alarm for a high-fall-risk patient to avoid noise, despite clear policy and knowing the risk, while staffing was adequate. Under Just Culture, the behavior is BEST classified as:

options.A: Human error, warranting consoling and a review of the system design
options.B: No issue at all, because the patient did not fall during that shift
options.C: At-risk behavior, warranting coaching only
options.D: Reckless behavior, warranting remedial or disciplinary action

questions.explanation_en: Conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk is reckless; the response targets the choice, not the outcome.
questions.explanation_ar: التجاهل الواعي لخطر كبير سلوك متهور يستوجب إجراءً تأديبياً.

questions.task_name: Apply techniques to enhance the culture of safety within the organization
questions.stem: A unit has high safety-culture scores for teamwork but low scores for 'communication openness.' Which intervention is MOST targeted?

options.A: Increase disciplinary audits so that staff follow communication rules
options.B: Reduce unit huddles to save time
options.C: Add more equipment and supplies to reduce frustration on the unit
options.D: Coach speaking-up tools (CUS) and have leaders welcome concerns

questions.explanation_en: Speaking-up skills plus leader responsiveness build psychological safety and communication openness.
questions.explanation_ar: تدريب أدوات التحدث بصراحة واستجابة القادة يعزز الانفتاح.

questions.task_name: Apply techniques to enhance the culture of safety within the organization
questions.stem: Which leadership behavior MOST strengthens psychological safety on a unit?

options.A: Posting names of staff involved in errors so others can learn from them
options.B: Thanking reporters and sharing what changed
options.C: Reviewing reports once a year
options.D: Rewarding the units that submit the fewest incident reports each quarter

questions.explanation_en: Feedback and appreciation for reporting reinforce a learning culture.
questions.explanation_ar: شكر المبلّغين وإطلاعهم على التغييرات يعزز الأمان النفسي.

questions.task_name: Integrate safety concepts throughout the organization
questions.stem: A board wants to make patient safety a strategic priority. Which action BEST integrates safety at the governance level?

options.A: Discuss patient safety at the board only after a sentinel event occurs
options.B: Make safety event rates and action status standing board items
options.C: Report only malpractice claims and their financial impact to the board
options.D: Delegate oversight to the risk manager

questions.explanation_en: Integration means safety measures and accountability are routinely reviewed at the highest level.
questions.explanation_ar: إدراج مؤشرات السلامة كبند ثابت في اجتماعات المجلس يدمجها استراتيجياً.

questions.task_name: Integrate safety concepts throughout the organization
questions.stem: A nurse involved in a fatal medication error shows signs of distress. What is the BEST organizational response?

options.A: Suspend the nurse immediately
options.B: Offer second-victim peer support and EAP services
options.C: Tell the nurse to keep working normally without any discussion of the event
options.D: Exclude the nurse from the event review to avoid further distress

questions.explanation_en: Supporting clinicians after harmful events is part of a mature safety program.
questions.explanation_ar: دعم الضحية الثانية من الزملاء والبرامج المساندة جزء من ثقافة السلامة.

questions.task_name: Integrate safety concepts throughout the organization
questions.stem: A hospital has a patient-family advisory council but it only reviews brochures. What change BEST integrates patients into safety?

options.A: Invite the advisors only to annual recognition and celebration events
options.B: Put patient advisors on safety committees and redesign teams
options.C: Disband the council
options.D: Limit the advisors to reviewing signage, brochures, and website text

questions.explanation_en: Meaningful partnership places patients in safety design and review, not just cosmetic tasks.
questions.explanation_ar: إشراك المرضى في لجان السلامة وإعادة تصميم العمليات عالية الخطورة.

questions.task_name: Integrate safety concepts throughout the organization
questions.stem: CANDOR and other communication-and-resolution programs emphasize what after patient harm?

options.A: Shifting responsibility for the outcome to the patient and family
options.B: Admitting fault only in writing after the legal team has reviewed it
options.C: Avoiding contact until litigation ends
options.D: Early disclosure, apology, investigation, and fair resolution

questions.explanation_en: Communication-and-resolution programs promote transparency and learning after harm.
questions.explanation_ar: برامج CANDOR تعزز الإفصاح المبكر والاعتذار والحل العادل.

questions.task_name: Use safety principles (human factors, high reliability, high-performance teams, systems thinking)
questions.stem: Look-alike vials of two high-alert drugs are stored side by side in an automated dispensing cabinet. Which human-factors fix is STRONGEST?

options.A: Separate storage plus tall-man lettering and distinct packaging
options.B: Post a warning memo about the look-alike vials on the cabinet
options.C: Add an annual competency on high-alert medications for all nurses
options.D: Tell nurses to read every label carefully before removing a vial

questions.explanation_en: Design changes that reduce reliance on vigilance are stronger than reminders.
questions.explanation_ar: فصل التخزين وتمييز العبوات أقوى من التذكير بالانتباه.

questions.task_name: Use safety principles (human factors, high reliability, high-performance teams, systems thinking)
questions.stem: Which high-reliability principle describes treating small failures as early warnings of larger system problems?

options.A: Sensitivity to front-line operations
options.B: Deference to expertise over rank
options.C: Commitment to resilience after errors
options.D: Preoccupation with failure

questions.explanation_en: HROs pay attention to near misses and weak signals as symptoms of system vulnerability.
questions.explanation_ar: الانشغال بالفشل يعني اعتبار الأخطاء الصغيرة إنذاراً مبكراً.

questions.task_name: Use safety principles (human factors, high reliability, high-performance teams, systems thinking)
questions.stem: A resident twice raises concern about a patient's unsafe discharge and is ignored. Under the TeamSTEPPS two-challenge rule, what should the resident do NEXT?

options.A: Discharge the patient as the attending physician ordered
options.B: Escalate up the chain of command
options.C: Accept the decision, since the concern was voiced twice already
options.D: Document the concern silently in the chart and take no other action

questions.explanation_en: After two unaddressed challenges, the concern is escalated up the chain of command.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد تحدّيين دون استجابة يُصعّد الأمر لمستوى أعلى.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: safety event/incident reporting
questions.stem: A patient receives a double dose of a vitamin supplement and has no harm. How should the event be classified?

options.A: No-harm event
options.B: Adverse event with harm to the patient
options.C: Sentinel event requiring a comprehensive review
options.D: Near miss, because the dose was only a vitamin supplement

questions.explanation_en: The error reached the patient but caused no harm, so it is a no-harm event.
questions.explanation_ar: الخطأ وصل للمريض دون ضرر فهو حدث بلا ضرر.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: safety event/incident reporting
questions.stem: After introducing an easy one-click reporting form and feedback emails, near-miss reports doubled while harm events fell slightly. How should leaders interpret this?

options.A: Staff are making more errors
options.B: A healthier reporting culture with more to learn from
options.C: The new form should be removed because it inflates report numbers
options.D: Safety has worsened, so leaders should audit the units involved

questions.explanation_en: Increased near-miss reporting reflects trust and visibility of risk, not more errors.
questions.explanation_ar: زيادة بلاغات الأحداث الوشيكة تعكس ثقافة إبلاغ أفضل.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: safety event/incident reporting
questions.stem: Which feature MOST encourages staff to use an incident reporting system?

options.A: Timely feedback on what was learned and changed
options.B: Lengthy multi-page forms that capture every possible detail
options.C: Naming the person at fault
options.D: Reports reviewed only by Human Resources for follow-up

questions.explanation_en: Feedback closes the loop and shows that reporting leads to improvement.
questions.explanation_ar: التغذية الراجعة عن التغييرات الناتجة تشجع الإبلاغ.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: sentinel/unexpected event review
questions.stem: A patient dies unexpectedly after a wrong-dose insulin infusion. What should be done FIRST?

options.A: Care for patient/family, secure the pump and drug, prevent recurrence
options.B: Start the formal RCA meeting within the hour with everyone involved
options.C: Discipline the nurse who programmed the pump before anything else
options.D: Wait 45 business days, then take action once the RCA is complete

questions.explanation_en: Immediate actions protect patients and preserve evidence; formal analysis follows.
questions.explanation_ar: أولاً رعاية المريض والأسرة وحفظ الأدلة ومنع التكرار الفوري.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: sentinel/unexpected event review
questions.stem: Which team composition is MOST appropriate for a sentinel event review?

options.A: Only the hospital attorney, to protect the organization from liability
options.B: An interdisciplinary team with front-line staff and neutral facilitation
options.C: Only the risk manager, who is trained in event investigation methods
options.D: Only the staff directly involved, since they know exactly what happened

questions.explanation_en: Effective reviews include those who know the process plus leaders and neutral facilitation.
questions.explanation_ar: فريق متعدد التخصصات يضم العاملين في العملية ودعم القيادة.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: sentinel/unexpected event review
questions.stem: After a sentinel event review is complete, how should findings be shared?

options.A: Keep the findings within the review team only to protect privilege
options.B: Share the findings only with the patient's insurer and legal counsel
options.C: Publish the names of the staff involved so others understand the event
options.D: Share lessons and system changes widely while protecting confidentiality

questions.explanation_en: Organization-wide learning prevents recurrence elsewhere.
questions.explanation_ar: شارك الدروس المستفادة مع الوحدات المعنية مع حماية السرية.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: sentinel/unexpected event review
questions.stem: A hospital's sentinel event action plans are completed on time, but similar events recur in other units. What is the MOST likely gap?

options.A: Weak, local actions with no spread or monitoring
options.B: The 45-day deadline is too long
options.C: Staff are reporting too many events for the team to analyze
options.D: The events are random and cannot be prevented by any action

questions.explanation_en: Recurrence suggests weak, unit-limited actions and lack of spread and measurement.
questions.explanation_ar: تكرار الأحداث يدل على إجراءات ضعيفة ومحلية دون تعميم أو قياس.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: root cause analysis
questions.stem: An RCA team asks 'why' repeatedly: The wrong dose was given → the label was misread → the font was tiny → the vendor changed the label → no process existed to review new labels. Which is the root cause?

options.A: The vendor's font was too small to read safely
options.B: The nurse misread the label during a busy medication pass
options.C: No process to review new product labels before use
options.D: The wrong dose was given to the patient at the bedside

questions.explanation_en: The root cause is the deepest controllable system cause; fixing it prevents recurrence.
questions.explanation_ar: السبب الجذري هو غياب عملية لمراجعة الملصقات الجديدة.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: root cause analysis
questions.stem: Which RCA tool organizes contributing factors into categories such as people, equipment, environment, and procedures?

options.A: Run chart of events over time
options.B: Gantt chart of RCA action items
options.C: Fishbone (cause-and-effect) diagram
options.D: Histogram of event frequency by unit

questions.explanation_en: The fishbone diagram structures potential causes by category during RCA.
questions.explanation_ar: مخطط عظم السمكة ينظم العوامل المساهمة في فئات.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: root cause analysis
questions.stem: An RCA's action plan contains: 'retrain staff,' 'update policy,' and 'add a warning sign.' What is the BEST critique?

options.A: Remove the warning sign, since signs are ignored by busy staff anyway
options.B: The plan is strong and complete because it addresses staff and policy
options.C: All are weak; add system-level actions such as forcing functions
options.D: Add disciplinary action for the staff involved to strengthen the plan

questions.explanation_en: Strong RCA actions change the system rather than relying on memory and vigilance.
questions.explanation_ar: جميع الإجراءات ضعيفة؛ أضف إجراءات نظامية أقوى.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: root cause analysis
questions.stem: What should every RCA corrective action include to show effectiveness?

options.A: Names of the staff involved
options.B: Formal written approval of the actions from the patient's family
options.C: An owner, a due date, and a measurable indicator
options.D: A legal disclaimer protecting the hospital from future liability

questions.explanation_en: Accountability and measurement verify that actions were implemented and worked.
questions.explanation_ar: كل إجراء يحتاج مالكاً وتاريخاً ومؤشراً قابلاً للقياس.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: proactive risk assessment
questions.stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes FMEA from RCA?

options.A: They are the same tool, used by different departments under different names
options.B: FMEA is used only after sentinel events; RCA is used for near misses
options.C: FMEA is proactive (before failure); RCA is reactive (after an event)
options.D: RCA is used to predict future failures before new processes go live

questions.explanation_en: FMEA looks forward at what could fail; RCA looks back at what did fail.
questions.explanation_ar: FMEA استباقي قبل وقوع الخطأ وRCA تفاعلي بعده.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: proactive risk assessment
questions.stem: A hospital plans to open a new hybrid operating room. Which risk assessment is MOST appropriate before opening?

options.A: Retrospective chart review of past OR cases
options.B: Root cause analysis of previous OR events
options.C: Healthcare FMEA of the new processes
options.D: Patient satisfaction survey after opening

questions.explanation_en: Proactive risk assessment of new or redesigned processes is done before patients are exposed.
questions.explanation_ar: قبل افتتاح خدمة جديدة يُجرى تحليل FMEA استباقي.

questions.task_name: Safety and risk management: proactive risk assessment
questions.stem: In an FMEA, failure mode X has S=4, O=9, D=2 and failure mode Y has S=9, O=2, D=4. Both have RPN 72. Which should generally be addressed FIRST?

options.A: Both are equal, so the team can choose either one at random
options.B: Neither, because both RPNs are below a threshold of 100
options.C: X, because its occurrence score is higher than Y's occurrence
options.D: Y, because its severity is much higher

questions.explanation_en: With equal RPN, the failure mode with higher severity typically takes priority.
questions.explanation_ar: عند تساوي الرقم تُقدَّم الحالة الأشد خطورة.
